customer_acme_ops: Hey team — our security/compliance folks can't see the audit logs in the Console. When they go to Settings → Audit logs it either shows an empty list or a 403. They need read access to meet a compliance review tomorrow. Can someone check entitlement/role mapping?

Maya (Support): Sorry to hear that. Can you confirm a couple quick things so we can triage: org id, a user email that fails, and whether you use SSO (IdP) for logins? Also, does the user see a generic permission denied message or a specific 'entitlement' notice?

customer_acme_ops: Org ID is org_8765. The failing user is sarah@acme.com. We use Okta SSO. The UI shows: "You do not have permission to view audit logs. Contact your admin." No detailed error code.

Maya (Support): Thanks — uploading to the escalation queue. Assigning eng to validate entitlement flags and SSO claim mapping. @Jon (Eng) @Priya (SRE) FYI.

Jon (Eng): I'll start by reproducing with a support-admin token and checking the entitlement bit on the org record and the user's role mapping. Can you paste a screenshot of the UI or the network response? If you can run curl that's useful too. Example repro we use:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \"https://api.redwood-inference.prod/v1/orgs/org_8765/audit/logs\"
```

If the token lacks `audit:read` scope you'll get a 403. The console also blocks if `audit_log_enabled` on the org is false or if the user's mapped role doesn't include the audit entitlement.

customer_acme_ops: here's the fetch response from the browser devtools (redacted):

Status: 403
Body: {"error":"forbidden","reason":"entitlement_missing","missing":"audit_logs.read"}

Priya (SRE): That response is explicit — entitlement missing. Two main vectors: 1) SCIM/role mapping from Okta didn't assign the compliance/audit role, or 2) the org-level audit retention/entitlement flag is off. I'll check the org config now.

Jon (Eng): I pulled the org record: `audit_enabled: true`, but `audit_entitlements: []` (empty). Looks like the org feature flag is on but no users/groups are mapped to the entitlement.

Alicia (Security): On the IdP side we recently updated claim mapping — we should confirm the assertion contains the `groups` claim and that the SCIM push hasn't deprovisioned the "Compliance-Audit" group. If Okta removed the group membership, users won't get the role.

Maya (Support): @customer_acme_ops can you confirm Sarah is in the Compliance-Audit group in Okta and that group is included in the SCIM push?

customer_acme_ops: Yes — Sarah is in the group. SCIM shows the group with members. But we did rename the group last week from "Compliance-Audit" to "compliance-audit" (lowercase). Could that break mapping?

Jon (Eng): Possible — our SCIM mappings are case-sensitive in some places. I'm checking the tenant mapping table for org_8765.

DeployBot: [automation] audit_entitlement_sync job started for org_8765

Jon (Eng): Found it — the SCIM group name mismatch prevented automatic mapping. The org had a stale mapping for "Compliance-Audit" which no longer matched the new group label `compliance-audit`. I can apply a one-off mapping to rebind the group to the `audit_logs.read` entitlement.

Priya (SRE): Before we change mappings, note this customer uses retention entitlements too. We should not flip retention flags arbitrarily. We'll map the group only to the read entitlement and keep retention policy untouched. Also patch the SCIM name normalization later.

Maya (Support): Proposed remediation steps: 1) Add a temporary SCIM mapping for `compliance-audit` → `audit_logs.read` so Sarah regains access. 2) Ask customer to confirm access. 3) Add a runbook entry and push a small fix to accept case-insensitive names in mapping sync. 4) Follow up with the customer and update their support ticket.

Alicia (Security): I'm adding a note to the compliance policy: ensure group name changes require revalidation. Also will request an audit of recent mapping changes.

Jon (Eng): I've applied the one-off mapping in the tenant admin tool: `bind_group('org_8765','compliance-audit','audit_logs.read')` — leaving a trace in the audit trail.

DeployBot: [automation] mapping_update event recorded (id m-4421)

Priya (SRE): Can someone try the console now? If it's still 403, ask them to do a hard refresh and re-auth (SSO token must be reissued to pick up new claims).

customer_acme_ops: Confirmed — Sarah can see the audit logs in the Console now. Thanks! One remaining ask: can we export last 90 days? Their compliance review needs a 90-day export in CSV.

Maya (Support): Great. For export, the UI export button will generate a CSV up to 30 days by default. For 90 days we can run a privileged export. Jon/Priya — can you generate a 90-day export and provide a secure upload link?

Priya (SRE): Will do. Generating export for org_8765 covering 90 days. ETA ~ 20 minutes. Will upload to customer-specific S3 with presigned link.

DeployBot: [automation] export_job started (id e-9921)

Jon (Eng): Action items captured:
- (Jon) Patch SCIM sync to normalize group names (case-insensitive) and add unit tests — target next release.
- (Priya) Run the 90-day export and share secure link.
- (Maya) Update customer ticket, include repro and resolution steps and note mapping change.
- (Alicia) Add policy note and confirm on Okta side.

Maya (Support): I'll follow up with the customer in the ticket and confirm satisfaction. I'll also add a KB article: "Audit logs: troubleshooting SSO/SCIM mappings and entitlement errors" with the curl repro snippet and common error codes (403 + entitlement_missing).

customer_acme_ops: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Can you also confirm that retention settings (how long logs are kept) remain as we configured (180 days)?

Priya (SRE): Confirmed in org_8765 settings: `retention_days: 180`. The entitlement change did not alter retention.

Maya (Support): Closing loop: Sarah regained access after SCIM mapping fix. Export job completed and link delivered to customer's secure portal (ticket #SUP-4498). We'll track the SCIM sync patch in the next release. Marking this thread resolved unless anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
